summary:
I fixed items 1 to 3 in the tools. They are 6 commits on 6e224b8, branch t7 in P/t7/tools, HEAD 225a0de, status clean, no trailers.

- **Item 1:** a slot in the match form is now matched only by the fact the references hold at that position.
- **Item 2:** a new page check, pagecheck.js, compares step counts, heading numbers, list numbers and every a/an against the page.
- **Item 3:** the absent list now compares every position as a slot, and also catches a sentence dropped from one variation (DROPPED). This holds from scratch too.

Each of the check's attacks on items 1 to 3 now fails in both modes. Before the fix (6e224b8), the four item-1 attacks were accepted automatically, and the one-variation drop left no trace from scratch.

Sentence identity did not change, so nothing was re-keyed. In the reviewed mode the thirteen languages' ledger and block rows are identical to my baseline. ts and perl FAIL on purpose (ts's absent 'Return the entity name.', perl's 14 defects), as before. No class opened or closed. Four shared matches now name ts as their reference instead of go or clojure, with the same outcome. pagecheck finds nothing on any of the thirteen.

Full self-test at 225a0de: 266 controls, 0 failed, 1 moved (recheck go-tut-step4-dropped [scratch], as before). 31 of the 266 controls are mine, and sentence-removed-go-branch [scratch] now passes and has been taken out of moved.json.

Items 4 and 5 (done before me) pass the check's own attacks. Each falls to my own attacks: 2 of 3 on item 4, all 3 on item 5. I report these and did not fix them.

The README now has the new checks, what each can still be fooled by, and a step list for bringing a port onto a base whose sentences changed. That step list was not run end to end.

P/v33/tools moved to bfecda9 while I worked (and had uncommitted changes when I looked). That commit touches classes/ocaml, perl, rb and swift.json, which my last commit also touches. It touches none of my tool code, controls or README.

items.item: 1. A slot accepts any of the language's own facts
items.does: Each position of a reference skeleton now records which fact paths each reference's own text there is the value of. The required set for the position is the intersection across references (excluding the language under review). A language's text is masked as a slot only when it is the value of one of those paths, in addition to the earlier conditions (it is its own fact; no other language prints it there as plain text). Only the match form changes. Sentence identity does not, so verdicts, sentence ids and hand records are untouched.

items.control: controls/samefact.json, self-test part samefact, both modes. Each control must leave a class for a person with nothing accepted automatically. The four controls are the check's own attacks adapted to v33a text: swap-ok-err-zig, record-read-is-list-py, collection-is-hash-rb, comment-collection-is-list-rb.

items.sound_because: A position's fact is defined by what every reference prints there, not by the language's own value list. A language's own fact of another path stays literal and cannot equal a reference's slot. Another language's value of the same path is not the language's own, so it stays literal too. The intersection removes coincidences of one reference: py's `list` is both its collection and method.list, but ts's `array` is only the collection.
items.still_fooled_by:
Two cases remain.

1. A position where every reference prints one word for several facts. There the set keeps all of them, so a language's other fact among them passes. Measured: in 'X returns the entity and raises on failure; Y reads its record (a Z).', py and rb give the set {recordType, ref.container, ref.valueType.OBJECT, ref.direct.returns, ref.prepare.returns}. So ocaml's 'map' (its OBJECT word) where its recordType 'value' belongs has the same match form. My attack still opened, but only because that class is a reworded pair whose OLD side matches no reference pair. As an added class it would be accepted.

2. A printer's output that equals a reference's is still matched as before.

items.item: 3. A sentence dropped from every variation, and from one
items.does:
The absent list now compares SLOT forms: every position (code span, fact phrase, prose fact word, comment fact) is a slot, whatever fills it (ident.js slots). It works per variation, in two passes:
- ABSENT (nowhere): every reference of the language's style prints the sentence in a variation (every reference, for a language alone in its style), and the language prints it in no variation.
- DROPPED: every reference prints it in a variation, whatever its style, and the language prints it in other variations but not in this one. It must also be short by more than in every variation where it does print it, so a constant shortfall is a difference of place, not a drop. Without that rule zig's ent-none was a false alarm: zig's prepare returns an error union and prints no `.err` sentence where rust's Result does.

Both fail the one command until hand/<l>.json absent gives a reason: a string for an ABSENT entry, and { why, variations } for a DROPPED one, which holds only while those are the variations. selftest's ledger and recheck parts count a new unexplained absent entry as flagged, because the one command fails on it. handstale.js reads the object form.

Measured first, at 6e224b8 (attacks/drop.json): go's and c's branch sentence dropped from EVERY variation was already an absent entry in both modes, because the n-tools T2 rule holds go and c, each alone in its style, to the every-reference list. The first-half engineer's moved.json note said otherwise. The remaining hole was the one-variation drop from scratch.
items.where: ident.js slots(); classify.js run(): slotsBy per reference and variation with counts, mySlots, two passes (ABSENT on same, DROPPED on refs with shortfall/usualOf), reasonOf; summary.js 'DROPPED, NO REASON' line; handstale.js absent object; selftest.js flagged includes newAbsent. Commit c3a6ae4.

items.sound_because: A slot form cannot differ between languages because of a runtime's own token, so a sentence every reference prints is found in every language that prints it, whatever its printer. The per-variation comparison sees a drop from one variation without any recorded count, so it works from scratch. The shortfall rule only suppresses a drop that matches a pattern the language shows in variations where it does print the sentence.

items.item: Procedure for bringing a port onto a base whose sentences changed
items.does:
New README section 'Bringing a port onto a base whose sentences changed', in five steps:
1. Move the code: git rebase --onto NEWBASE OLDBASE in the port's clone. Conflicts can only be in the language's own files.
2. Build and declare the facts the new base made required (at v3.3: testMock and a truth read), then run the language's guard.
3. Take the new tools at the commit that goes with the base, with the language's records. Re-key with rekey.js (--from for v3.2 ids, --code for a later code); a second run must say 'already keyed'.
4. REGEN=1 portcheck, and read what is open by kind: classes the sentence changes opened (decided by the same written rule per changed template as the references: sfix/run/decide.py, v33/mine/decide.py), STALE, RECOUNT, ABSENT/DROPPED, UNATTESTED.
5. Run until PASS, then once with SCRATCH=1.

The old paragraph is marked superseded.
items.sound_because: Step 1 is the step the check's literal run lacked. Its 16 open classes were the old base's sentences still printed by the port's code.
items.still_fooled_by: Not run end to end. All four wave-1 ports are already merged into v33a, so no port remains on an older base to move.

bring_in:
P/v33/tools has moved since I started: it is now at bfecda9 ('Thirteen languages decided after the shared decisions ...') and had uncommitted classes/*.json changes when I looked. bfecda9 touches classes/*.json, counts/rb.json, hand/*.json, normalizers/rb.js and purity-allow/{perl,rb}.json. It touches none of my tool files, controls or README. My last commit, 225a0de, touches classes/{ocaml,perl,rb,swift}.json, which bfecda9 also changes: drop 225a0de and regenerate classes instead.

Commands, with export PATH=/opt/node24/bin:$PATH:

```sh
T=/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/f1977c62-4748-5872-8f72-6f448dbac3f1/scratchpad/design/proto2/t7/tools
cd <frozen tools> && git fetch $T t7
git cherry-pick 3c4d27e 987c52a c3a6ae4 549635a 0e61496   # NOT 225a0de
```

Expected conflicts: none in code. README.md only if the frozen README changed near 'For a port started from v3.2: move it onto the current clone FIRST'; keep both texts.

Then:
1. Run the thirteen: `for l in ts go py c zig clojure rust elixir rb perl swift ocaml lua; do ./portcheck.sh <clone> <out> $l; done` (REGEN=1 on the first). Commit the regenerated classes/*.json as their own 'classes as generated' commit.
2. Run the full self-test (the command under selftest), about 26 minutes alone on the machine.

What the engineer must decide:
- A new 'DROPPED, NO REASON' or 'ABSENT, NO REASON' entry, if the shared engineer's sentence changes remove a sentence from some variations of a language: give a reason in hand/<l>.json absent ({ why, variations } for a dropped one), or fix the page.
- Any class that opens because a language's text is its own fact of another path than the references hold: decide it by hand. At v33a there were none.
- Any pagecheck finding: a page that is wrong (no hand record can accept it).
- If shared sentences change, the controls in samefact.json, pages.json and missing.json name exact page text: an ERR 'text to inject not found' means a control must be re-targeted to the new text and recorded as adapted.
not_done: Did not fix my own attacks on items 4 and 5: a staged file deleted from the project, a source with its time set back, a loose OLD marker, correction records quoting OLD as NEW, and quotations found only in another language's components. Each is reported with its fix under done_before_me.

Did not close the item-1 case where every reference prints one word for several facts (py/rb `dict`/`Hash` = recordType, container, OBJECT, direct/prepare returns). A position-level rule cannot separate those paths without a marker in shared code saying which fact it substituted.

pagecheck does not judge an article before a symbol-led code token (102 in go), checks no number other than step counts, heading numbers and list numbers, and does not catch a heading renumbered by a change of level.
The DROPPED pass compares only sentences every reference prints; a sentence 8 of 9 references print is not covered. go-tut-step4-dropped [scratch] stays moved.
The README port procedure was written but not run end to end: no port remains on an older base, because the four wave-1 ports are in v33a.

I did not re-run the check's full attacks1.json list through attack.js, because the classify-only harness cannot see pagecheck. Its item-1, item-2 and item-3 cases are covered by my controls and attack runs.
No compiler was used; none was needed for these tools.
surprises: The first-half engineer's moved.json note said go's and c's branch sentence dropped from EVERY variation leaves no trace in either mode. At 6e224b8 it was already an absent entry in both modes, because n-tools' T2 holds go and c (each alone in its style) to the every-reference list. Only the one-variation drop from scratch was still open.

Item 1 opened no class in any of the thirteen languages: every shared match at v33a is a same-fact-path match. Four matches name a different reference (ts instead of go or clojure) with the same outcome.

My first per-variation drop rule gave two false alarms on correct pages:
- zig ent-none: zig's prepare is an error union, so it prints no `.err` sentence where rust does;
- rust no-test: zig prints 'with mock features active', and rust's testMock is 'generated'.
The shortfall rule and comparing drops against every reference removed both.
pagecheck's first article rule flagged 97 correct 'a `NULL`-terminated array' lines in c. NULL is read as a word, not spelled out.
One rb portcheck in dev2 had its fact sheet terminated from outside my run, probably another engineer's process cleanup on the shared machine; a rerun passed.
I edited tools/ident.js while the baseline's go run could read it. I reverted at once, re-ran go (identical), and did all later work in a separate worktree.
